issue.body:
Can timeout and scheduling changes recover complete positive control pairs without repairing tasks? Follow-up to #28; investigation remains open.

**Completed:** four existing Matchms exports now have positive nop/oracle pairs, preserved regression tests and clean oracle commands; all 40 task files are unchanged. These are completed controls, not new exports. [Results](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/188091eb/experiments/29-runtime-limits/matchms-control-results.json).

**Scanpy:** replaying all 16 recorded bootstrap commands reproduced their original exit codes, including a failure that stops the generated Dockerfile. No command or dependency repairs were made. Smoke/fresh-image checks remain false, so this is reconstruction evidence, not environment readiness or original-image equivalence. The unchanged PR4389 export is now submitted for nop/oracle controls at 300 versus 1,200 verifier seconds. [Replay evidence](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/65cfc8b5/experiments/29-runtime-limits/scanpy-recorded-result-001.json) · [Control protocol](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/65cfc8b5/experiments/29-runtime-limits/scanpy-controls-protocol.md).

**Remaining:** verify the Scanpy controls and cleanup; assess faithful OHIF reconstruction (its Docker build excludes a required workspace); run the separate OpenMS checkout comparison; checkpoint MMseqs2’s bootstrap comparison and model allowance. The OpenMS timeout option is prepared but not live-tested. Longer verifier limits cannot resolve installation or checkout failures.

**Budget and retention:** eight completed jobs used 1.06233 allocated CPU-hours. The submitted controls allow at most 9.6667 more within the existing 32-hour ceiling, on reserved capacity. Zero model calls. One owned Scanpy image remains for these controls and will be removed after archive readback. Raw Matchms evidence remains private. No pipeline promoted. Detailed logs and execution updates remain in comments.

comment_body:
🤖 **Scanpy recorded-command replay completed.** All 16 BASH actions matched their original exit codes, including the system-pip failure followed by the original venv commands. No commands, dependencies or task files were repaired and no model was called. This resolves the saved Dockerfile’s stop-at-first-failure reconstruction barrier; it does not reproduce the deleted original image bytes.

The original smoke and fresh-container checks still return false, with collection errors. [Verified replay result](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/65cfc8b5/experiments/29-runtime-limits/scanpy-recorded-result-001.json) · [Archive readback](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/65cfc8b5/experiments/29-runtime-limits/scanpy-recorded-readback-001.json). The replay used 0.42267 allocated CPU-hours; cumulative measured #29 use is 1.06233 hours across eight terminal jobs. Its containers, checkout and downloaded tooling were removed. One owned image is retained for the scoped controls.

Submitted `biotasks29-scanpy-controls-001` on the same reserved worker: the original Scanpy PR4389 package, all 10 files hash/mode verified, nop/oracle at 300 and 1,200 verifier seconds. Harbor 0.6.6, 1 CPU/6 GiB, original grading/tests and internal timeout retry semantics stay fixed. [Exact comparison and cleanup protocol](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/65cfc8b5/experiments/29-runtime-limits/scanpy-controls-protocol.md). The one-attempt 8,700-second job has a 9.6667 CPU-hour maximum within the existing 32-hour ceiling. No new capacity or model calls. Results remain pending; the retained image will be deleted after archive readback.

Separately, the OpenMS checkout option is prepared and passes config/command-parity checks: default 60 seconds, configurable to 300, unchanged clone/fetch limits. This is synthetic validation only; no live OpenMS checkout comparison has started. [Candidate patch](https://github.com/Open-Athena/biotasks/blob/8ae98a2f/experiments/29-runtime-limits/checkout-timeout.patch).
